html:
A hymn whose title means "Lord, bless Africa", written in 1897 by Enoch Sontonga, a Xhosa teacher and choirmaster at a Methodist mission school in Johannesburg. More verses in Xhosa were added later by the poet Samuel Mqhayi.

Mission choirs spread it across southern Africa. The African National Congress sang it at its meetings from 1912 and made it its anthem. During the struggle against apartheid it was sung at rallies and funerals, and the government saw it as a song of protest.

It became a national anthem in several countries:

  • Tanzania and Zambia use its tune with their own words.
  • In 1997 South Africa combined it with the old anthem, Die Stem, in five languages, as a sign of reconciliation.

Zimbabwe and Namibia also used it for a time after independence.
